audits.title: A prospective audit of the implementation of the 2-week rule for assessment of suspected urological cancers.
audits.standard: UK Government 2-week rule for suspected cancer referrals (seen within 2 weeks); regional tumour working group referral criteria
audits.setting: Department of Urology, St Helier Hospital, Carshalton

cycle1.result: 82/234 GP referrals met regional suspected cancer criteria; 13% clearly marked urgent/cancer; 23% had no implication of cancer; 72% seen in haematuria clinic with median 56.5 days and none within 2 weeks; others median 21 days with 34% compliance.

audits.other_findings: DoH figures recorded only 18 referrals over 3 months with 89% compliance, grossly underestimating the true workload.
audits.citation: Coxon JP, Harris HJ, Watkin NA. A prospective audit of the implementation of the 2-week rule for assessment of suspected urological cancers. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2003;85(5):347-350. doi:10.1308/003588403769162486. PMID: 14594541.

audits.title: Audit of referrals for head and neck cancer - the effect of the 2-week, fast track referral system.
audits.standard: NHS Cancer Plan: maximum 2-week wait from suspected cancer referral to outpatient appointment via fast track
audits.setting: South Essex region head and neck service (St John's Hospital, Chelmsford)

cycle1.result: 71% of patients diagnosed with head and neck cancer were not referred via the fast track; only 15% of fast track referrals had cancer.

audits.other_findings: Cancer patients referred by standard letter generally waited much longer than 2 weeks.
audits.citation: Lyons M, Philpott J, Hore I, Watters G. Audit of referrals for head and neck cancer - the effect of the 2-week, fast track referral system. Clin Otolaryngol Allied Sci. 2004;29(2):143-145. doi:10.1111/j.0307-7772.2004.00744.x. PMID: 15113298.

audits.title: An audit of urology two-week wait referrals in a large teaching hospital in England.
audits.standard: Department of Health two-week wait referral guidelines for suspected urological cancer
audits.setting: Urology department, Russells Hall Hospital, Dudley; large teaching hospital

cycle1.result: 42 (11%) referrals were inappropriate. Cancer found in 90 of 400 (23%); detection ranged from 50 of 122 (41%) for elevated PSA to 2 of 56 (4%) for scrotal lumps.

audits.other_findings: Most inappropriate referrals were for long-standing symptoms and non-specific testicular or scrotal symptoms; authors suggest GP access to fast-track scrotal ultrasound.
audits.citation: Mathew A, Desai KM. An audit of urology two-week wait referrals in a large teaching hospital in England. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2009;91(4):310-312. doi:10.1308/003588409x391767. PMID: 19344552.

audits.title: Urgent suspected cancer referrals from general practice: audit of compliance with guidelines and referral outcomes.
audits.standard: Agreed national urgent suspected cancer referral guidelines
audits.other_findings: Referral rate ranged 3.7 to 24.0 per 1000 per year; many referrals outside guidelines still had cancer (urological 15.9%, lung 8.8%).
audits.citation: Baughan P, Keatings J, O'Neill B. Urgent suspected cancer referrals from general practice: audit of compliance with guidelines and referral outcomes. Br J Gen Pract. 2011;61(592):e700-6. doi:10.3399/bjgp11x606591. PMID: 22054333.

audits.title: Two audits of the diagnosis of oral cancer and the two-week rule following referrals from primary care practitioners in Newcastle.
audits.standard: Department of Health two-week rule referral guidelines
audits.setting: OMFS department, Newcastle General Hospital, then oral surgery and oral medicine, Newcastle Dental Hospital

cycle1.result: 57 (90%) seen within time; 60 (95%) conformed to guidelines; cancer detection rate 11% (7/63).

audits.intervention: Repeat identical audit in a different department; no intervention described.

cycle2.result: 43/49 (88%) seen within time; 39 (80%) compliant with guidelines; detection rate 7%.

audits.other_findings: All patients with cancer had guideline-compliant referrals; further education of referrers recommended.
audits.citation: Miller CC, Hierons RJ. Two audits of the diagnosis of oral cancer and the two-week rule following referrals from primary care practitioners in Newcastle. Prim Dent Care. 2012;19(2):63-68. doi:10.1308/135576112800185241. PMID: 22507147.
